title: Babel-Ashur · Keeping a Foothold
dek: Shelter becomes a responsibility: follow the survivors, divided defenses, mountain assault and mist rescues through the people who carry their consequences.

facts.Reading scope: Selected quest scenes and compatible Refuge history
facts.Dates: Source postings; not an established in-world calendar
facts.Last stage: October mist rescue; lasting safety unconfirmed

body:
On Babel-Ashur, a place to hide becomes a place people depend on. That change makes each expedition answer a harder question: how can the company strike at danger without leaving the people behind it exposed? Follow the people and choices below to see why a saved shelter, a shattered mountain and a rescued party are different achievements.

1 · A shelter becomes a responsibility

Skylight Refuge offers water, plants, a narrow approach and a concealed cavity beneath the sky. Those features let people survive; they do not make a fortress. Aravil names basic work such as reconnaissance, hunting and materials. Aerrow fears that noise and traffic will reveal the camp, while Arjahn sees people whose courage makes the place worth defending.

The June rescue widens that responsibility. Living captives are brought out and a golden seed is entrusted to Elenia. At the later meal, Kvethe, Quille, Omari and Kyrin speak about broken continuity, lost land and what remains to protect. Kvethe wants safety for the children while refusing to abandon her homeland. An offer to leave does not mean an evacuation has happened.

The place people depend onSkylight RefugeWater and concealment must become care, supplies and defensible shelter.Read their history →Custody and obligationEleniaKeeping the seed does not settle when, where or whether it can safely be planted.Read their history →Addressing a survivorArjahnHe apologizes for speaking around Kyrin and offers help without promising to repair every wound.Read their history →

Keeping that shelter supplied requires repeated journeys beyond concealment. The Mark of the Wild hunting history follows the gathering work, failed harvests, retreats and losses beside the larger expeditions.

2 · The defense divides, and survival has a cost

When hunters find the Refuge in August, the company splits its work. Olokun, Elenia and Scribonia draw danger away. Arjahn, Eugene and Nymera stay with the civilians. Choosing a battlefield away from them reduces one risk without making the defenders safe.

Eugene’s desperate Wish destroys two attackers; Nymera is found dead among the remains, and Arjahn explicitly brings her back with Revivify. He then apologizes for speaking as if he could abandon her. The relief is brief. The diversion returns with wounded companions and pursuers, and Nymera is reduced to ash during the next fight. Eugene and Scribonia finish the attackers. The narrator records the Refuge as safe, with a person still lost.

Eugene gathers the ashes at Elenia’s request. Her later restoration attempt and Nymera’s subsequent living presence continue the history; they do not turn the second death into the first Revivify or supply an unrecorded spell name.

Spending what remainsEugeneThe cautious defender becomes a desperate caster and still needs help afterward.Read their history →Duty meets attachmentArjahnCivilian priorities do not make losing a companion bearable.Read their history →Holding, returning, holding againNymeraHer two deaths belong to two different moments of the same defense.Read their history →

3 · From holding ground to breaking the stronghold

The later mountain offensive grows from continued pressure, while the companions give different reasons for it. Elenia wants room for healing; Scribonia develops the weather plan; Eugene questions the consequences; Arjahn openly names vengeance. These motives coexist. None guarantees the plan will spare people hidden below.

Eugene and Scribonia sustain separate weather systems. Elenia and Arjahn redirect water and break the mountainside with earthquakes. Flooding, avalanches, fissures, smoke and lava visibly change the stronghold. Arjahn carries Eugene out when the water threatens the casters themselves.

The result is an altered mountain and a successful withdrawal. Those witnesses cannot yet know every casualty or whether Abyss is permanently destroyed. October’s later encounter answers the question of his continued activity without giving them that knowledge in advance.

Helping while questioningEugeneHe sustains the storm, worries about its consequences and depends on another person to escape.Read their history →Vengeance beside careArjahnHis desire to destroy does not erase his rescue of Eugene.Read their history →Outcome and uncertaintyThe mountainVisible destruction does not certify a complete victory or account for every civilian.Read their history →

4 · A test makes the next danger clearer

The September gathering begins with work and warm tea rather than a declaration that the island is saved. At the coast, the company encounters a field of unstable magic at the Luminar Spires. Elenia’s Daylight becomes reversed gravity, forcing companions to solve a danger created by their own experiment.

The green mist remains a separate problem. Gartina observes figures, Elenia attributes its arrival to a rift and Arjahn tests radiant power. The opening closes again. Proximity does not prove the Spires caused the mist, and an amplified spell does not establish that the same method will make a safe passage.

Results before explanationsLuminar SpiresRead the altered spell, rescue and bounded tests together.Read their history →Methods and alternativesGartinaObservation, practical proposals and rescue matter beside spectacular magic.Read their history →

5 · Rescue becomes the danger

By October, ordinary wildlife has returned around the Refuge, but the route beyond it remains dangerous. Ryvyt’s preparation helps Olokun survive the salamander ambush. The company then reaches the coast and tries to investigate the advancing mist.

Personal lures break the tethered plan. Arjahn, Wren, Olokun and Nymera perceive urgent threats to people they love; rescuers become apparent enemies. Their experiences are real distress without establishing that the depicted people are physically there.

Ryvyt frees Nymera with Dispel Magic before Scribonia’s Wish clears the wider area. Greater Restoration and wind have more limited or failed results. The rescue belongs to several distinct attempts and contributions, rather than one remedy that explains everything. Abyss appears and withdraws, establishing continued activity after the mountain assault.

Preparation and changing remediesRyvytHis successful dispelling precedes the wider clearing.Read their history →A rescue beyond self-protectionScriboniaA ward protects his own mind without making extraction simple.Read their history →Searching for someone elseWrenThe attempt to help exposes her own commitments to the mist.Read their history →

6 · Getting people home is part of the outcome

The clearing does not repair every relationship. Wren remains angry after Scribonia slaps her and dismisses an experience she could not control. Arjahn apologizes for the failure of his protection without promising he is beyond the same vulnerability. Nymera receives care and reassurance, then becomes the person carrying Scribonia when he collapses.

Death’s offer is met with questions and refusals. His later assertion about Aria remains a claim beside her witnessed death; the encounter does not show her return. The company’s reactions do not turn any received vision into independently established history.

Wren supplies food. Arjahn escorts Nymera and Scribonia toward the Refuge. The surviving packet ends on that assisted return, with recovery still ahead. Shelter matters because victory can leave people needing somewhere safe to be hurt, rest and disagree.

Care moves in both directionsNymeraThe companion freed from the mist helps carry someone else home.Read their history →Returning to careOlokunNeeding rescue does not end his responsibility to others.Read their history →A place to recoverSkylight RefugeLocal improvement and an exhausted company can be true together.Read their history →

What this foothold has not settled

The seed’s planting, durable defenses, the mountain’s full casualties, the mist’s lasting removal and the second restoration’s exact means remain open. A returned companion does not retroactively explain the spell that brought her back. Nor does a later enemy appearance reveal everything that happened in the earlier assault.

Follow the remaining evidence questions, the island history or the chronology. The dates throughout this path locate source postings rather than declaring Fenumion’s calendar.
